activity_context.topic_title: The Integral as an Accumulation Function

feedback.worked_solution:
Evaluating $F(x)$ at $x=3,$ we get the following definite integral:

$$
F\,(3)={\int }_{1}^{3}(4t-3)\,\text{d}t
$$

Then, computing the definite integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}F(3) & ={\int }_{1}^{3}(4t-3)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(2{t}^{2}-3t)\,{|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =(2\cdot {3}^{2}-3\cdot 3)-(2\cdot {1}^{2}-3\cdot 1) \\  & =(18-9)-(2-3) \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$
